messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft onramp playbook + TPM targets for Novus Retail

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, I put together an initial onramp playbook that ties the evaluation milestones to a staged commit and monthly TPM targets so we can align incentives and discounts to adoption. Attached is a lightweight MAP that maps the P0 evaluation goals to milestone acceptance criteria, the proposed monthly token trajectory, and illustrative pricing.

High level ask: can you review the MAP and confirm whether the acceptance gates and the proposed monthly TPMs line up with your internal success criteria? Notable points we’d like your feedback on:
- Month 1: 500k tokens (pilot) to validate throughput and latency SLOs
- Month 2–3: ramp to 3M TPM with prefix cache enabled and Q4 optimization
- Discount ladder tied to hitting 80%/90% of target for two consecutive months

Attachments: Novus_MAP_draft_20250914.pdf, proposed-pricing-tpm-v2.xlsx

If we can agree on MAP milestones this week, I’ll circulate a clean SOW + proposed invoice schedule for procurement.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
v: 415-555-0183

Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft onramp playbook + TPM targets for Novus Retail

Vanessa —

Appreciate the quick turn. Looping in our procurement lead for any contract-level questions. Initial read looks reasonable but a couple of items from the Novus side:
1) Month 1 pilot: Can you lower the pilot TPM to 250k for the first 30 days? The pilot will only ly in scope for two storefront teams, not the whole org.
2) Discount triggers: We need a clearer definition of what constitutes "hitting" a TPM target (rolling 30-day average vs calendar month).
3) We may need an escrow/credit protection clause if we go beyond 6 months with a ramp commit.

I’ll review the MAP with the engineering lead and get back with specific acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director of Product
Novus Retail

Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft onramp playbook + TPM targets for Novus Retail

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick notes and for pulling procurement in. Two quick replies inline:
1) Pilot TPM: We can reduce Month 1 to 250k TPM to match the two storefront teams — that will lower cost for the pilot while keeping the environment representative for latency and KV cache behavior.
2) TPM measurement: We recommend a rolling 30-day average (compute windowed avg) for a smoother signal and to avoid calendar month edge cases; happy to make it calendar month if procurement requires it.
3) Escrow/credit protection: We have standard credit hold and early-termination terms; for ramp commitments >6 months we can add a mutual break clause tied to quarterly business reviews. I’ll have legal draft language once we land the numbers.

Next step: I propose we update the MAP with the reduced pilot TPM and add a short appendix defining the TPM measurement method. If that’s OK I’ll share an updated MAP + a draft SOW with billing milestones.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novus MAP — pricing & discount ladder implications

Team —

Quick pricing note after reviewing Jordan's ask. If we accept Month 1 = 250k TPM and a conservative ramp to 3M by Month 3, the economics change and we'd want to adjust the discount ladder thresholds to protect unit economics. Proposed tweak:
- Base price holds for months 1–2 (no discount) to recoup onboarding cost
- 6% discount when rolling 30-day avg >= 70% of target for two consecutive months
- 12% discount at >= 90% of target for two consecutive months

Also propose a success credit of $10k if Novus achieves 100% of Month 3 TPM within 45 days of the Month 3 start — this helps align incentives and smooths procurement conversations. See attached pricing workbook for modeled P&L.

Rishi
Head of Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: proposed-pricing-tpm-v2.xlsx)

Thanks for the clarity. Procurement reviewed the commercial model and has two points:

- The success credit is interesting but will need to be reflected as invoice credit that applies only after acceptance of Month 3 ramp metrics.

From an engineering acceptance perspective, we’ll confirm the P0 criteria this Monday and expect to have the definitive acceptance gate language by 9/22.

Jordan

Subject: Final MAP update + SOW milestone schedule (draft)

Jordan —

Per your feedback, we updated the MAP: pilot TPM = 250k (Month 1), measurement = calendar month (per procurement), and success credit structured as an invoice credit applied after verified Month 3 acceptance. I attached the revised MAP and a draft SOW with billing tied to three milestone checkpoints: pilot acceptance, ramp-to-3M acceptance, and end-of-quarter performance review.

We also added an appendix clarifying "accepted" traffic (rolling live storefront sessions, test harness excluded) and a short operational runbook for key contacts and escalation paths.

Next steps: If procurement confirms the calendar-month measurement and the invoice-credit construct, I’ll ask legal to put together the SOW + contract redline. Would you prefer DocuSign or a traditional counter-signed PDF for execution?

Thanks,
Vanessa
